messages.author: 156a0be20e5567ba
messages.subject: Automatic stopping
parts:
Hi,

is there a possibility to tell Stan to automatically adjust warm-up and number of iterations based on the statistics?
Something like:
"I am interested in having a rough heuristic that burn-in is over. And then I am interested in getting a certain number of effectively independent samples"
Maybe based on the statistics that Stan is able to extract from finished chains? If not, that would be *great* to have. I am using Stan for experiments with 1000s of chains with all different posterior distributions, and I would like to have some mechanism that roughly stops all of them at an appropriate time, similar to the way it automatically tunes the HMC parameters to each posterior.

Thanks a lot for your thoughts a great tool!
Heiko

messages.author: 156a0be20e5567ba

"I want M independent samples from the model"
I am aware that this is literally impossible to do properly, but as said, an automated heuristic would be fine.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Automatic stopping
parts:
I'm not sure about the other interfaces but in R, the thread is taken over by the sampler and doesn't release until all the chains are finished. Conceivably, you could call R from C++, but if you are doing chains in parallel, I don't think the output gets flushed back into the memory of the main R process until the chain is finished. Although Andrew likes such ideas, I don't think we have worked out what a good stopping rule would be, even if it were feasible to implement.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Automatic stopping (time-based runs, multi-threading, sharing warmup)
parts:
That would be nice, but there are several obstacles as Ben points out.

The primary issue is that convergence is monitored based on
generating enough post-warmup iterations that R-hat converges.

Without some serious innovation, the best idea we have is to run
warmup, then run samples after that, then monitor convergence, and
if not converged, go back to warmup. This is actually related to your
earlier question.

The technical issue is cross-chain communication, which pre-C++11
is a huge pain for portability (Boost threading might help, but then
it's not header only and introduces more compilation issues). When we
move to C++11, things should get easier. Right now, the chains just
run independently.

For now, the best thing to do is something like this:

num_iter = 100;
while (num_iter < MAX_ITER) {
run Stan in 4 chains for num_iter iterations;
if converged break;
else num_iter *= 2;
}

At most, this is going to take only around twice as long as optimal.

The other idea Andrew wants to explore (and which I think sounds like
a good idea) is to do time-based runs. That requires a mixed-length chain
version of R-hat and n_eff. This addresses the issue of variability in
time taken across chains, which now can be up to an order of magnitude in
some cases. You can reduce the variability with smaller initial step sizes
and higher acceptance probabilities, but that slows things down. We haven't
done anything like a rigorous set of testing on this.

There's also the possibility to share warmup information across chains.
Because Stan right now with Euclidean HMC adapts a global mass matrix,
this should be the right thing to do.

- Bob
